versioned_original_source_to_ssc.source_review_disposition: Source edition, title, author and abstract heading. No additional mathematics.

Taking Euclidean Spin4=SU2L times SU2R fundamental assigns right factor to proposed gravity and left factor to part of standard gauge fields; Lorentz reconstruction needs chosen time-direction degree interpreted as Higgs.
Conformal compactification R4 to S4 identified with HP1, tautological H right-handed spinor bundle, and Euclidean PT=CP3 over HP1 with CP1 fibers are distinct typed carriers.
Fiber complex line C inside H selects tangent complex structure R4 regarded as C2; author's Higgs/time-choice degree needs to be a PT field in this C2.
CP3 is said to supply U1 times SU3 pointwise internal symmetry; fermion generation transformation properties are described as simple expressions on PT, not quantified or dynamically constructed here.
Author explicitly says proposed unification geometrically encodes symmetries but needs further gauge theory and spinor field quantization formalism on PT rather than spacetime.
Introduction heading.
Definition problems in Minkowski theory are sometimes, not always, addressed using analytic continuation from Euclidean signature.

Minkowski noncommuting equation-of-motion operators and free Wightman distributional holomorphic boundary values contrast with commuting Euclidean fields, no equation of motion, and free Schwinger actual functions.

Minkowski states can be covariantly defined; Euclidean construction chooses imaginary time and OS reflection to define state space and Lorentz-invariant inner product, perpendicular to the path-integral state hypersurface.
Reverse Minkowski-to-Euclidean continuation has infinitely many Euclidean slices, individually chosen by imaginary time direction; SU(2,2) real form is determined by signature-(2,2) Hermitian Phi.
Phi-null locus in PT is real dimension five; its projection to tau=0 S3 inside compactified S4 depends on imaginary time parameter choice.
Minkowski physical states carry SL(2,C) simple group action; Euclidean Spin(4)=SU(2)L x SU(2)R is a two-simple-factor product and does not act on physical states in source's stated comparison.
Appendix B is cited for previous signature issues; gauging spacetime symmetries is suggested as an approach to quantum gravity but remains problematic between the signatures.
Author proposes Euclidean four-dimensional QFT as fundamental and claims gauging SU2R chiral spin connection can formulate Einstein equations.
SU2L is assigned internal weak interactions, yielding part—not all—of the Standard Model gauge fields after gauging.
Author requires selected imaginary time to break Spin4 for Minkowski reconstruction, enabling distinct SU2R/SU2L roles and proposing a Higgs degree of freedom dependent on twistor theory.
Penrose's 1967 twistor work [32] is cited as prior origin, alongside author's qualitative evaluation of the spinor explanation problem in conventional geometry.
Minkowski point is a complex 2-plane in T=C4 with tautological Weyl-spinor degree and claimed parity asymmetry; PT=CP3 is instead complex lines in T.
Conformal transformations are described as linear maps on twistor vector space C4.
G_(2,4)(C) consists of complex 2-planes and jointly complexifies, without identifying, Euclidean and Minkowski real signature constructions.
The source proposes naturally occurring Standard Model internal roles and prints CP3=SU4/(U1 times SU3), previously conserved in W005 including its exact source-printed quotient.
Author assigns internal U1 and SU3 at projective twistor points, separately distinguishes U1 times SU2 on the lifted imaginary-time/Higgs candidate; previous W005 has two typed source statements.
